title: Aiden and Betty: New Teeth
reason: Simplify over-complex prose, explain normal baby-tooth loss accurately and gently, and correct the false description of Socks the dog as a primate.

pages.1: Aiden bit into an apple. One front tooth gave a little wobble. He touched it gently. "My tooth is loose!" he said.
pages.2: Betty looked with a small torch. "It is a baby tooth," she said. "It will fall out, and a new tooth will grow."
pages.3: That night, Aiden felt worried. Losing a tooth seemed strange. Socks sat by his desk while Aiden thought about it.
pages.4: Mum said loose teeth were normal. "Everyone loses baby teeth as they grow," she said. Aiden felt a little better.
pages.5: At lunch the next day, Betty lost a tooth too. She looked at the tiny tooth, then wrapped it in a clean tissue.
pages.6: "Did it hurt?" Aiden asked. "Only for a moment," Betty said. She smiled at the new gap in her teeth.
pages.7: On Thursday, Aiden's tooth came out while he was reading. It was quick, and it did not hurt.
pages.8: The tooth was tiny. Aiden put it in a small envelope. Then he tucked the envelope under his pillow.
pages.9: In the morning, the envelope was gone. A coin lay under the pillow. Aiden smiled. Mum smiled too.
pages.10: Three weeks later, a new tooth began to grow in the gap. It looked bigger than his baby teeth.
pages.11: "You do not look strange," Betty said. "You look a little older." Aiden looked in the mirror and smiled.
pages.12: Socks sniffed near Aiden's smile. Then he sniffed near Betty's. He was curious about their new tooth gaps.
pages.13: "Soon we will both have new teeth," Aiden said. Socks wagged his tail. The gaps did not bother him at all.
